title: Meshy
author: Dangerous_Three_8506
selftext:
How many of you guys are using Meshy?

I am thinking of buying it but I am hesitant and poor. I've got money as a gift I can use for it but I don't know how well it works.

When you use meshy how many other products do you use with it?

I want to do game design as a hobby and the meshy tool looks like it would make my hobby way easier. 25$ of codex plus meshy and my own work.

I didn't really want to do the art myself and with the rise of easier game development I am excited to make my own game where its my personal joy to play all day.

My main question is this, do you use Meshy plus something else? Or just meshy? Do you use an alternative? I don't want to make my own art, the AI allowed me to have a new hobby.

comments.author: IcyBother8850
comments.body: I use Meshy, for my 3D isometric game, models look OK plus you can add several basic animations which come quite handy, Ofcourse you will need to normalize and polish stuff in blender but Id say 80-90% of the job is done by Meshy.

replies.author: Dangerous_Three_8506
replies.body: You have a lot of blender experience? I learned about scripts lately, you use that stuff?

replies.author: IcyBother8850
replies.body: Not really I post screenshots of blender to GPT and let it guide me what to do, scriots are fine as fire and forget but for the stuff I want to learn I do the screnshots in blender with instruction by chatgpt, its a more tedious process but at the end you can do them on your own after the first 1-2 examples by gpt

replies.author: Standard_Text480
replies.body:
How do you get consistent sizes and themes without meshy re inventing its style? for example i want to make 30 leagues of legends style characters all the same size

then say i want to change one characters weapon

replies.author: IcyBother8850
replies.body: You do the concept art in the same style in GPT for example, only after you are satisfied will all concept art only then you create the models...for weapons if you are using 3D you need to render the model empty handed then add hand socket in blender then attach weapon to that socket

comments.author: FTWGames
comments.body:
Used it for a 3d project I was prototyping and experimenting worflows. Like it has been said on this post: use a GPT or whatever source image to feed into Meshy and it will produce a decent model. You can fiddle with poly counts and a few other variables to eventually have animations as well. Also enjoyed 3d models generated with Meshy for other aspects of the prototype like items, decor, etc.

The flow that worked for me is feed an Image to Meshy, then to Blender for clean up (AI can coach you step by step on this), then to Mixamo for rigging and animations.

That said, unless you can’t find what you are looking for in paid or free assets, Meshy is one of many options to generate assets.

comments.author: PhotojournalistBig53
comments.body: It does a decent job. I still use it primarily for low impact props like stones, mountains, bridges, lamps, crates, interior things. I do think Tripo does a better job with low poly mesh concepts. You can also get blender and learn to clean the models and fix the textures to get truly great models if you are low on cash but high on time. Blender is free and you'll control it manually mostly, the ai models aren't good at it (yet) but they are a great teacher for it.

comments.author: Some-Mistake8113
comments.body: ChatGPT Sol on High has been good at procedural generation through Blender MCP. You can make them in batches and tell ChatGPT to generate the materials. Just made 16 buildings in a few hours. Just kept telling it what to fix- have it save the recipes. It’s not good for characters though. That’s where Meshy shines. Just need to make some skills in Claude code that know how to properly simplify and repair assets. Have it experiment and probe the assets until it gets a good result.

replies.author: Some-Mistake8113
replies.body: https://preview.redd.it/fdzfnl1qlcnh1.png?width=1174&format=png&auto=webp&s=0019a0931df630bc09e50d6f74ea218f73c12768

replies.author: Dangerous_Three_8506
replies.body: That's blender? How much work did you do with Chatgpt?

replies.author: Some-Mistake8113
replies.body: That building is inside an app I’m making (that’s the lighting and environment). The building itself was made entirely with ChatGPT Work. I first generated seamless materials that can tile in every direction, then I connected ChatGPT to Blender MCP while it built out the 16 buildings. Each time I saw something wrong, I told it what to correct and improved it over the course of a few hours. Because I had it make it in a batch, any time I fixed one thing on one building, it fixed it on all of them. Then I shipped it to my app and imported it, and added the lighting.

replies.author: bettertagsweretaken
replies.body: What skills have you found for Claude that help with Blender?

replies.author: Some-Mistake8113
replies.body:
I built my own. Basically, the prompt went like this:

I want to create a set of skills, each one specializing in building certain kinds of 3d models using Blender. Each time you build a model and I correct you, I want you to improve the skill that made it. I also want the skills to save the procedural recipes that made the skill after I approve the model. The goal is to create an organized library of methods to create each kind of object. First, have several subagents research blender techniques for procedural generation and create a core library for each skill that gives it a good starting point. Be thorough and accurate and double check your work.

comments.author: EchoingAngel
comments.body:
How messy are the things you are making? Any transparent parts? Do you need to animate these things?

Meshy is actually pretty decent if things don't have flat surfaces and aren't see-through. Once you need clean surfaces, glass, or movement, you're going to have issues.

Rodin is what I use for "cleaner" assets. I've also used Tripo for a couple assets. None of them are insane, though and there is a ceiling of how good things will look (and a much lower ceiling for how clean their topology is)

comments.author: irschdon
comments.body:
have been using meshy for 3D asset generation for a few weeks now. tried tripoAI before, but switched for the a) better quality and b) imo slightly better subscription model for meshy. 

Whats your game like? As I have quite minor animation requirements the auto rigging for humanoid fantasy beings works very good for basic stuff. If you can do it yourself its very good to refine or use Sol5.6 /Fable5.1 to pick that up and refine aswell. 

I looked at a few other comparable services, but my main issue with all is that you cant locally/partially adjust generated assets with a prompt. Meshy offers 12x free retry for each asset (which is a lot, I usually max use 3-4 for a very good result), but in some niche occassions it can be annoying that you gotta redo the whole thing instead of just adjusting a minor detail. 

Hint for tripo and Meshy, and most likely comparable competitors: create a free account (logically), try it out; then buy the baseline subscription. use the credits (its not that much) and check out the sub upgrade options. In my case, I had 40% offered by Tripo (which i did not get anyways) and i think it was 70% offered by Meshy when i upgraded, and that makes quite a difference.
